messages:
incident-bot: Pager: S3-egress-route 503 spike (P3) -- ~120 errors/min to embeddings proxy from hosted-api (region: us-west-2). Alerted at 20:02 UTC.

maya: I saw the pager. I’m primary on shift. quick summary: started at 20:02, spike peaked ~20:06. Not all customers affected; mostly large-batch embedding calls.

ravi: I’m on standby as secondary. I can take network-side checks and load-balancer rules.

jules: Notified infra team; I’ll check whether any recent deployment touched the embeddings proxy or the egress ACLs.

maya: Initial triage:
- 20:03: checked proxy logs, lots of 502/503 from downstream egress nodes.
- 20:04: kb: connection resets to embeddings svc (10.12.8.*).
- 20:05: autoscaler for embeddings pool scaled up but new instances got same errors.

maya: Hypothesis: egress path (NAT/gateway) is intermittently dropping long-lived connections under high burst from bulk-embed jobs. Rate pattern matches large clients.

ravi: I ran curl test from a host in same AZ: got 503 with chunked response headers.
Command:
```
curl -v https://embeddings.internal.redwood/v1/encode -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{"inputs": ["x"]}'
```
Response snippet: `HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable` then connection reset.

jules: No infra deploys in last 3 hours. No ACL changes in cloud console logs. There is a network policy change earlier today in a staging account — verifying if config drift occurred.

maya: Mitigation steps taken so far:
1) Added a temporary routing rule to send traffic for embeddings to fallback pool in another AZ (us-west-1 fallback).
2) Throttled large-requests via API gateway for 10m to reduce burst (policy: max_batch_tokens=5000).
3) Opened ticket with cloud provider for egress errors (case #CLOUD-5841).

incident-bot: Note: automated rollback detector detected no recent model rollout. No auto-rollbacks executed.

dana: After routing to fallback pool (20:12) error rate dropped to ~15/min. Latency on fallback is +120ms but stable.

maya: Customer impact: partial; high-volume batch embedding jobs experienced retries/timeouts. Several enterprise customers hit backoff. No data loss.

ravi: Current status (20:20 UTC):
- Error rate: 12/min (was 120/min)
- Fallback routing active
- Autoscaler stable
- Cloud support case open, SOC notified for possible infra incident

maya: Next steps for oncall handover:
- Maintain fallback routing until cloud provider confirms egress stability OR until we can validate NAT gateway metrics are normal.
- Remove API throttle only after error rate < 2/min for 15m.
- Post-incident commit: add circuit-breaker in gateway and per-tenant batching limits.

maya: Who’s taking first watch for next 4h? I’m handing to @jules as primary for 20:30–00:30 UTC, @ravi as secondary.

jules: I’ll take primary. Planning: monitor provider updates, watch connection reset metrics, verify no config drift across accounts.

ravi: I’ll be secondary, will keep an eye on LB and NAT gateway metrics and be available for escalations.

maya: Coverage notes / gaps:
- We don’t have an automated end-to-end test that simulates sustained bulk-embed bursts across AZs — add as follow-up.
- Runbook for egress flaps is sparse. Linking runbook we referenced: https://redwood.runbooks/egress-flap (internal).

opsrunbook: Runbook pointer: see section "Fallback routing and throttles" + run commands:
```
# check gateway errors
kubectl -n infra logs -l app=egress-gw --tail=200 | grep "reset"
# verify fallback routing
curl https://console.redwood/api/v1/routing/status?service=embeddings
```

maya: Action items (owners):
- jules: validate cloud provider packet captures and confirm root cause (owner: jules)
- ravi: add LB/NAT alert thresholds for connection reset count (owner: ravi)
- dana: compile list of impacted customers and send advisory if needed (owner: dana)
- maya: draft postmortem outline and schedule follow-up review (owner: maya)

jules: I’ll post updates in this thread after cloud provider reply. If anyone sees error rate creep >30/min, escalate to oncall pager and route to dedicated capacity for critical customers.

maya: Leaving shift at 20:30 UTC. Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:

jules: Acknowledged — picking up.

incident-bot: Thread tagged: handoff, mitigation-in-progress, followup-required.
